main_text.p: se, quam est, absque divinæ naturæ mutabi-litate. Idem omnino est actus volendi secundum rem, qui sine ulla mutatione ad varia terminatur, & idem actus prout ad hoc termi-natur volitio & est odiū. Nec sunt ulli in Deo, ut in nobis actus vere contrarii aliquid reale ad-dentes: quare iidem fuissent actus decretorum Dei, qui nunc sunt, & eodem modo se ha-buisset essentia Dei, quo nunc se habet: si qui jam reprobi, fuissent electi, & qui jam electi, reprobi. Nam libertas in creaturis est ad actus indifferentes: in Deo vero est ad alia tantum atque alia objecta extra se, & hinc videre possunt Arminiani, quomodo immuta-bilitas Dei cum absoluta libertate consistat.

2. Nos vel accuratoribus Jesuitis & Scholasticis litem amandamus. An Arminiani digna divinæ majestatis ter tremendâ immutabili na-tura doceant, qui ut hæretico Vorstio & suo genio lenocinentur, statuant multos esse actus li-beros in Deo, qui nunquam in eo fuissent, nisi antecederent humanæ & angelicæ quædam vo-litiones. Sed ad rem, præsentem disquisitio-nem ad duos fontes revoco, ad Arminiana placita de præde­stinatione, & de justificatione, & [illegible, ~14 letters] εἰς τὸ ἀλληγορῶ[?] exercitationes scribenti lectori dabit veniam, si nostram doctrinam de justificatione obiter vindicare tentavero.
3. 1. Forensis illa distinctio electionis in peremptoriam, completam & irrevocabilem, & non peremptoriam, incompletam & revo

page.notes: Running head and catchword are as printed; the catchword "cabi" begins the next word "revocabilem" and is the only catchword. The Greek phrase after "&" in paragraph 2 is not legible to me letter by letter; the portion "εἰς τὸ ἀλληγορῶ" is my best reading and is marked [?]. "tremendâ" carries a doubtful mark over the final vowel. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept as shown ("mutabi-", "immuta-", "na-", "fuissent" etc. as printed). Long s is rendered as plain s throughout; s appears in the source only as the printer's long s and is normalised. The soft hyphen in "præde­stinatione" marks a line-end break that I could not confirm; the word is probably "prædestinatione" without a printed hyphen.
